item.title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
item.description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

item.title: Jennifer Lopez claims not being a ‘typical’ White actress made it harder to land Hollywood movie roles
item.description: Jennifer Lopez claims Hollywood overlooked her as a Latina actress, saying she had to create her "own lane" as critics push back on social media.
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Lopez is receiving criticism after claiming that she has struggled to land acting roles in Hollywood because she is not White, describing how she has been forced to create her "own lane" as a Latina entertainer, in an interview published on Friday.

Lopez made the remarks in an interview with The New York Times, pushing back on the notion that she gets thousands of acting offers, claiming instead that Hollywood has often overlooked her because of her ethnicity.

"Even from the beginning of my career, I got offered things, but I was only offered a few things. I had to kind of create things for myself," the actress said. "And the reason, I think, is because I just wasn't the typical kind of, like, to be honest, a White actress. You know what I mean? And it's still kind of the same today."

'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD AFTER YEARS OF REJECTION AND ‘ABUSE’

Lopez’s more recent film credits include "Office Romance" (2026), "Shotgun Wedding" (2022), "Hustlers" (2019) and "Second Act" (2018).

She also secured several leading roles in the late 1990s and early 2000s, including "The Wedding Planner," "Out of Sight" and "Maid in Manhattan," and was cast as the late singer Selena Quintanilla-Perez in "Selena."

JENNIFER LOPEZ ADMITS SHE 'WOULD'VE HAD SEX' WITH ENTIRE STAR-STUDDED 90S MOVIE CAST

The Puerto Rican actress said Hollywood continues to look for "certain" things when casting performers, suggesting that the industry's preferences have historically made it more difficult for actors of color to secure roles.

Lopez acknowledged, however, that the screen industry has made progress in improving diversity and representation.

"There's a certain thing that they look for, and it's more diverse now for sure, and that's good," the actress said.

"But because of that, you have to kind of create your own lane in a lot of ways," she added. "If I want to do something, I don't wait for somebody to offer me…I try to do it, and then if something comes along, great."

IDRIS ELBA REJECTS 'WOKE' JAMES BOND CASTING PUSH, WARNS AUDIENCES 'WON'T GO FOR A BLACK MALE' IN THE ROLE

Fox News co-host Tomi Lahren pushed back on Lopez’s claims, writing on X: "LOL, sure Jan."

Internet personality Oli London noted Lopez’ robust net worth and catalog of big-screen appearances, writing on X: "JLO has appeared in 44 films and is worth $400 million."

Actress and "America's Next Top Model" personality Adrianne Curry-Rhode also chimed in, calling Lopez' comments "next level delusion."

"You are old now. You were a bad actress, but very hot...that's why you got casted," Curry-Rhode wrote in a post to X.

Movie critic Christian Toto told Fox News Digital, "Lopez has worked steadily over the past two decades, bouncing from major film projects to concerts and her solo music career. She's undeniably talented and has earned every gig that came her way. Still, for her to suggest she's been penalized by Hollywood for the color of her skin is absurd. How many out-of-work actors would kill to snag a fraction of the work Hollywood has sent her way?"

item.title: Solo diners are asking restaurants for half-size portions, sparking debate over menu flexibility
item.description: Solo dining is up 22% year over year, and some chefs will happily make half orders so diners alone can try more dishes without wasting food.
item.content:encoded:
As solo dining continues to surge in popularity, there is debate over whether it’s acceptable for guests dining alone at a restaurant to request a smaller portion size of a dish.

Reservations for one saw a 22% increase year over year in the third quarter of 2025, according to a report from restaurant technology company Toast.

One appealing part of dining out with a group is sharing plates and trying bites of many different dishes.

RESTAURANTS DRAW THE LINE ON SUBSTITUTIONS AS DINERS PUSH MENU LIMITS

Solo diners who still want to sample a variety of items without having an overwhelming amount of food on their table may be able to do so by simply asking their server if they can place a half-order, Food & Wine reported.

Opinions are divided online about whether this is an acceptable request, with some believing that it’s no big deal while others say it’s not worth it.

"Don't even bother, order the regular meal. And when it comes, you eat what you want of it, and anything that you have left over, get a to go box and take it home," one person wrote on Quora.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Many restaurants don’t appreciate when an adult orders a smaller portion size, the commenter added, saying, "they consider it to be a waste of their cooking time to make small portions for an adult."

Plus, they noted, it doesn't hurt to have leftovers.

Some chefs are happy to serve smaller portions to a solo diner because they want them to have a positive dining experience and be able to try many different dishes without wasting as much food, Food & Wine noted.

"It never hurts to ask!" another Quora user said, with the caveat that certain dishes are more easily re-portioned than others.

"Whether or not you are successful in your request depends on a few things. If the dish is pre-proportioned, then it’s not likely," they noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

For example, if an entree contains a half lobster tail, it’s probably not likely that the kitchen will scale that component down, the commenter continued, adding that restaurants may refuse to serve whole fishes and meats, portioned desserts or pizzas in smaller sizes.

The important thing for diners to remember, they said, is that they will probably pay full price for a dish even if it’s a half-sized portion, because it takes an equal amount of time and effort to make.

One Reddit user agreed that the portion sizes of certain dishes are more easily adjusted than others.

"I think it’s easier with pasta dishes because they can portion out the amount of pasta, sauce, garnish, etc and keep selling the rest. Not so easy with a piece of protein (1/2 steak, 1/2 fish filet, 1/2 burger) because those are generally pre-portioned for service," they said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Another person noted that they wanted a smaller portion to reduce food waste — and a smaller bill would be nice, too.

"I hate wasting food, but if I eat the full portion I’m overeating and will feel sick. I’d love to do a half portion for a slightly cheaper price and not overeat or waste food," they said.

One Redditor shared that they were pleasantly surprised when a restaurant they dined solo at charged them half of the menu price for a half-sized portion.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries calls Trump chief of staff Stephen Miller a ‘stone-cold racist,’ refuses to sit down with him
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries said he refuses to meet Stephen Miller, calling him a "stone-cold racist" and slamming his role in the Trump administration's mass deportation agenda.
item.content:encoded:
Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., declared firmly on Saturday that he will not sit down with White House chief of staff Stephen Miller — calling Miller a "stone-cold racist" while mulling over who his conduit to the White House will be.

Jeffries, who is set to become House speaker in January, made the remarks during a recent podcast interview with The New York Times, in which he discussed ways he plans to work with the Trump administration to move forward legislation for the American people. When asked whether he imagined sitting across from Stephen Miller, Jeffries firmly said, "No," and disparaged the White House official.

"I've made it clear that Stephen Miller is a stone-cold racist. Why would I deal with him at this point in time?" Jeffries said. 

TRUMP'S MOVE FROM WILES TO MILLER SIGNALS MAJOR TACTICAL SHIFT FOR GOVERNING WITHOUT CONGRESS

Jeffries, who has historically been an outspoken critic of Miller, said he cannot meet with someone who has carried out such a violent immigration agenda.

"This is the architect, the architect of Donald Trump's violent mass deportation machine. And there's cruelty associated with that. There's chaos. In fact, there's death associated with what's taking place," Jeffries said.

In response to Fox News Digital, White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers defended Miller's track record.

"Unlike the hardcore, partisan Democrats who refused to work with the President and blocked many of his popular policies, Stephen Miller has a track record of spearheading bipartisan efforts: public safety reform, making our cities such as Washington, D.C., and Memphis safe again, drug pricing transparency, and unleashing a nuclear energy renaissance," Rogers told Fox News Digital.

JEFFRIES VOWS DEMOCRATS WON’T ‘GIVE A DIME’ TO TRUMP’S DEPORTATION EFFORTS

TRUMP TELLS DHS CHIEF TO WORK WITH DEMOCRATS ON IMMIGRATION REFORM, BUT NO AMNESTY

When President Donald Trump appointed Miller, Jeffries also blasted the president’s move as an "irresponsible decision" and condemned the chief of staff for his movement to "brutalize and kill American citizens," referencing the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good during immigration enforcement actions.

Trump defended the deportation agenda of his chief of staff pick at the time, telling Kayleigh McEnany on "Saturday in America" that, "The one thing with Stephen – he was very strong on the border."

"So, he called him a racist. But we had to be strong," Trump continued. "They allowed 25 million people and killers, murderers. They allowed drug dealers and rapists into our country."

The president also lauded Jeffries as a "very smart" and "reasonable guy."

"What he did is pretty spectacular with getting that position," Trump said. "And it’s nice – first Black person in that position. It’s a big deal."

THE MISTAKE NEWLY-ELECTED DEMS ADMIT THEY CAN'T AFFORD TO MAKE WITH TRUMP AFTER SWEEPING 2026 WINS

Jeffries insisted to The New York Times that his refusal to meet with Miller was "not a boycott," and expressed that he was willing to have an open communication line with Trump, just not Miller.

"I think practically speaking, one, I can communicate directly with the president," Jeffries told The New York Times. "I mean, everybody seems to have his number, but the president is not a hard person to reach."

Jeffries also said he can take his issues to Vice President JD Vance, explaining that in prior administrations, engagement between congressional leaders and the White House oftentimes happened via Cabinet secretaries or vice presidents.

The New York Democrat declared he will "maintain a willingness" to work with politicians across the aisle to get things done for the American people.

Jeffries’ office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Week 12 AP Top 25 Poll sees Big Ten powers rightfully punished while Longhorns jump the Crimson Tide
item.description: Texas surged back into the AP Top 25's Top 5 after UCLA and Indiana fell on the road, while Alabama fans fume over the Longhorns' late-season inside move.
item.content:encoded:
After the Week 11 AP Top 25 poll was an anomaly, with the top nine teams going unchanged from the week prior, we returned to our regularly scheduled programming of utter chaos in college football and a lot of moving pieces in the newest edition of the AP Top 25 poll.

The Big Ten suffered some untimely cannibalization in Week 12, with Indiana, UCLA, and Ohio State all going on the road and losing, and all three teams were punished rather harshly as a result.

The SEC scoreboard featured nothing but chalk this past weekend, but with the Big Ten producing a mess, Texas has entered the Top 5 again, which can't be sitting all too well among Alabama fans.

GEORGIA HAS TOP COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF SEED IN SIGHT WITH DOMINATING ROAD WIN OVER NO 21 SOUTH CAROLINA

With voters being forced into putting out a fresh set of rankings every week for three consecutive months, they appear to have found their stride, at least as best they can. Remember, voters are spread out all around the country, in different time zones, making it physically impossible to watch even the extended highlights of every meaningful game on the slate.

With that in mind, there isn't a whole lot to get too worked up about when it comes to the upper echelon of this week's rankings.

UCLA has been a great story this season, and the sport is better when the Bruins are relevant, but they've undoubtedly felt like the team primed for a slip-up, and that coming to a Michigan team that is inept on offense is pretty peak college football.

The Bruins tumbling from No. 4 to No. 10 after having their unbeaten season ruined in Ann Arbor is fair. They're still a one-loss Big Ten team, and one-loss Big Ten teams deserve to remain inside the Top 10 this season.

LANE KIFFIN TAKES THE SIDE EXIT AS TENNESSEE SENDS LSU HOME AND MOVES TO THE DOORSTEP OF CFP

Indiana went from a one-loss Big Ten team to a two-loss Big Ten team after an unsuccessful trip to Washington. The Hoosiers may only have one meaningful win all season – against USC in Week 11 – but their two losses have come by a combined seven points. Plus, Ohio State was still Ohio State when Indiana lost at home to the Buckeyes in October.

Everyone would rank the Hoosiers ahead of Iowa, Oregon, and USC in the Big Ten, which is exactly what the AP voters did this week.

The Longhorns dominated a 4-6 Arkansas team 45-3 on Saturday, and it was exponentially more impressive than Alabama's 47-0 win. It's incredible that sentence is factual, but it is, seeing as how Alabama's shutout came against FCS Chattanooga.

FIFTH-RANKED TEXAS DOMINATES ARKANSAS AS ARCH MANNING IS HEATING UP AHEAD OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

Texas, Alabama, and Tennessee all sit at 9-2 on the season, and the Longhorns getting inside the Top 5 after UCLA and Indiana fell is inarguable. The Longhorns beat Tennessee earlier in the year, and the schedule broke with Alabama's cupcake game coming in the penultimate week of the season, hence the inside move on the Crimson Tide.

A week ago, the Longhorns were No. 8 while Alabama was a spot ahead.

The AP Poll is irrelevant due to the College Football Playoff Rankings ruling all, meaning the back end is even more pointless, but it gives college football fans something to argue about and argue we will.

Last week, voters elected to keep Ole Miss ranked at No. 25 after losing to Oklahoma. Florida was also ranked No. 23 a week ago. The Sooners beat both the Rebels and Gators earlier in the year, but did not have a number next to their name in Week 11.

Suddenly, a week too late, Oklahoma has surged to No. 19 ahead of the Gators and Rebels.

We can't just pick on the SEC teams when it comes to the back end of this week's poll, because what on Earth is Boise State doing at No. 22?

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The Broncos lost 22-20 at home to what was a 5-5 San Diego State team on Saturday night for their second loss of the season.

Liberty, at No. 21, is the lone non-Power Four team that should be inside the Top 25, but we as a society decided long ago that 'the little guy' has to be shown preferential treatment, and internal fighting among voters may have broken out if only one Group of Five team had a number next to its name this late into the season.

item.title: DK Metcalf disqualified from Steelers game for unsportsmanlike penalties including poking opponent's facemask
item.description: DK Metcalf's frustration boiled over vs. the Philadelphia Eagles as a jawing match with Cooper DeJean escalated into an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.
item.content:encoded:
DK Metcalf is clearly frustrated about this season because he's not producing as expected and on Sunday we saw what could be a full manifestation of that frustration when he was disqualified from the game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The incident happened in chapters on consecutive Steelers' drives and culminated with 4:58 left in the third quarter when Metcalf seemed to poke the facemask of Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean.

DK METCALF WILL NOT FACE CRIMINAL CHARGES FOR VIRAL ALTERCATION WITH LIONS FANS

This fracas was away from the play and even after the play was over. But officials caught it, and disqualified Metcalf for picking up his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the third quarter.

Officials called Metcalf for an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty because, they said, he was taunting DeJean. The Eagles contend Metcalf poked DeJean in the facemask.

The previous possession by the Steelers offense, Metcalf had gotten into a kerfuffle with DeJean and been flagged for his first unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

We have no idea what led to this little brouhaha between Metcalf and DeJean. On the first play, Metcalf turned a block of DeJean into a push, during which he grabbed DeJean by his neck and then the front of his collar.

DeJean (6-foot and 198 pounds) then grabbed the bigger Metcalf (6-4 and 235) around his collar and the two men started pushing on each other.

But Metcalf was apparently very hot because he could be seen jawing at DeJean even as other Eagles and, eventually, Steelers players joined the fray.

(By the way, NFL moments like this are a sportswriter's dream because they allow for the use of words such as kerfuffle, brouhaha and fracas).

Anyway, as the two men were locked onto each other's collars, officials joined the tussle and pulled each player away.

Except that when the game umpire stood between Metcalf and his ability to rejoin the rumpus, he put a hand on Metcalf's chest.

And Metcalf swiped it away – which is surely about to get the NFL's attention beyond the disqualification.

Anyway, Metcalf was penalized for unnecessary roughness as his first offense.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

So Metcalf went to the locker room with more personal foul penalties (2) than catches (1), and he cost the Steelers more yards by penalty (19) than the yards he contributed via his catch (1).

NFL SUSPENDS BUFFALO BILLS SAFETY CJ GARDNER-JOHNSON AFTER GROTESQUE SPITTING INCIDENT

Metcalf is supposed to be Pittsburgh's top receiver but had only 35 catches for 432 yards and 2 TDs in nine games coming into Sunday's action.

One more thing: Metcalf has something of a history as a hothead.

During the 2025 NFL season, Metcalf was suspended for two games without pay by the NFL for initiating a physical confrontation with a fan during a Week 16 game at Ford Field against the Detroit Lions on December 21, 2025.

item.title: TCU fires Sonny Dykes after giving him a spring extension, and fans' reactions say it all
item.description: TCU football fired head coach Sonny Dykes after a 38-17 loss to the Utah Utes, with AD Mike Buddie citing a slide from the Horned Frogs' Fiesta Bowl peak.
item.content:encoded:
Seven months after handing Sonny Dykes a massive extension, the powers at TCU decided they'd seen enough.

The program let go of the TCU football head coach Sunday, a day after the 38-17 dismantling by the second-ranked Utah Utes.

Athletic Director Mike Buddie issued the school's statement, nodding to the 2022 run before laying out the slide since.

Saturday marked TCU's final home game of the season.

"Since 2022, however, the Frogs have posted a 28-21 overall record and a 17-18 mark in the Big 12 while finishing or ranking 10th or worst in penalty yards per game within the league each of the past four seasons," the statement read, in part.

"After appearing in the Big 12 Championship Game in 2022, TCU has finished an average of 7th in the league standings since. With Saturday's result, the Frogs currently sit in 12th."

"While Sonny's tenure began with the incredible achievement of winning the 2022 Fiesta Bowl and advancing to the national championship game, the proceeding years have seen our program slide further away from that mountain top than can be accepted," Buddie said.

"I am grateful to Sonny for his belief in TCU, his family's love for the Fort Worth community, and for his coaching staff's commitment to recruiting and developing men of high character."

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT

"TCU's investment in football has led to dramatic growth of our university and city in the past 20 years, and we cannot allow that investment to fall short of its due return, especially at such a pivotal time of change in college sports.

"We expect to compete for Big 12 championships, to be a central figure in the College Football Playoff conversation, and our continued investment and growth potential reflects that. I expect our new leader will echo those sentiments, rally our fan base behind that challenge, and put a team on the field that our alumni, fans, students, and community will be excited to support."

Dykes’s five-year stint in Fort Worth opened with a 12-0 regular season behind Max Duggan and a 51-45 Fiesta Bowl upset of Michigan; then the carriage turned to a pumpkin in a 65-7 national championship loss to Georgia.

Despite posting 9-4 seasons in 2024 and 2025, a 5-7 slump in 2023 and a 5-6 mark in 2026 sealed his 41-23 tenure.

After his dismissal, TCU fans largely anticipated and accepted the move after a stretch of uneven seasons. Reactions on X happily capped the Dykes era.

Some memes featured Dave Aranda and Brian Kelly (jokingly) as candidates for the vacancy, while one person suggested Shane Beamer, not so jokingly.

"He absolutely caught lightning in a bottle in 2022, and they’ll never reach that height again," one reaction read.

More poured in. "Couldn’t wait until after Thursday? Some of us need the Frogs locked in against Texas Tech."

Another reacted, "Kinda crazy TCU had the balls to do it."

Some took issue with TCU's decision-making on the extension's financials.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S MEGA ROSTERS AREN’T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON PROVE

"They extended him in spring for no reason whatsoever. But paying players is what makes CFB broken."

OutKick Sr. college sports reporter Trey Wallace gave his first impressions, reading the tea leaves on TCU's next move.

"They are going to swing for the fences. Could USC head coach Lincoln Riley be interested if things continue trending in that direction in LA? Baylor is interested, so what about TCU? "

"A number of names will be interested because of how much TCU is willing to spend in hopes of contending in Big 12 and for CFP spot. They can attract hot names around the sport, and wouldn’t have fired Sonny Dykes if they didn’t already have a few names in mind."

"They will owe him $20 million after giving him an extension in April," Trey noted.

item.title: Landry Kiffin was not dressed for the golf ball rain that fell during Lane's return to Knoxville
item.description: Landry Kiffin says she "wasn't dressed for it to rain golf balls" as Tennessee fans threw mustard and golf balls at Neyland Stadium during LSU's loss.
item.content:encoded:
If it's been said once, it's been said a thousand times, when you're handed an ugly loss, turn it into content. Those apparent lessons in content that Landry Kiffin is receiving from Livvy Dunne are paying off.

Fresh off a trip to New York City this week with the former gymnast, Landry was in Knoxville on Saturday as LSU took on Tennessee. It was a family affair for the Kiffins as Lane made his return to one of his former teams.

To say that Volunteers fans have no love for the LSU head coach is an understatement. It's a relationship that, given how Lane's time at Tennessee and his exit played out, won't ever be repaired.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Fans showed up in mustard costumes, had profanity-laced chants for the LSU head coach, and were packing golf balls. They even made Lane and the Tigers leave the field through the side exit.

Those golf balls weren't simply props. They eventually came raining down on the field along with bottles of mustard as fans threw them while Tennessee handed LSU it's fifth loss of the season by the score of 27-13.

Those weren't conditions that Landry was prepared for. She was prepared either way to make content out of it, but on Sunday she admitted on Instagram, "wasn’t dressed for it to rain golf balls."

LSU'S LANE KIFFIN HANDS TENNESSEE BULLETIN BOARD MATERIAL, CLAIMS HE FORGOT HE EVER COACHED THE VOLS

Her content mentor chimed in on the post. Livvy Dunne wrote in the comments, "Still ate despite the hazardous conditions."

You can't let hazardous conditions keep you from eating. Just like you can't let a failure to live up to the hype keep you from pretending as if you're a college football powerhouse.

That's what you do when you show up on Saturdays.

Now Landry's experience at Neyland Stadium wasn’t without some controversy. She posted a video on TikTok of Tennessee fans chanting about Lane that she's since deleted.

It was captioned "Rent free" and included text that read "Incase ur wondering what the unemployed sound like."

You win some, and you lose some when it comes to producing content too. But whatever you do, you keep moving forward.

That's what Landry did and, with the people she's surrounded herself with, it's hard to expect anything less.

item.title: 'I Dream of Jeannie' star Barbara Eden, 95, still rides exercise bike for 35 minutes to stay fit
item.description: Barbara Eden reveals the stationary bike routine and personal trainer workouts keeping her fit as the "I Dream of Jeannie" star turns 95.
item.content:encoded:
Barbara Eden isn’t slowing down at all — she's actually speeding up.

Despite turning 95 in August, the "I Dream of Jeannie" icon stays fit by working out on her stationary bicycle.

"I go for about, I don't know, 35 minutes on the bike," Eden told Fox News Digital recently of her fitness routine. "It's good."

BARBARA EDEN, 95, SAYS SHE’S ‘OKAY’ AFTER LAST-MINUTE CANCELATION OF FESTIVAL APPEARANCE

The former sitcom star said that both she and her husband of 35 years, Jon Eicholtz, both have a personal trainer who comes to their home.

"I don't go to the gym anymore," she revealed, adding that when she did, it was "spinning class for an hour, and then I worked with a trainer for a half hour, lifting weights."

DONNA MILLS DOES 100 SIT-UPS A DAY, PLAYS TENNIS FIVE TIMES A WEEK AT 85 BUT WON'T QUIT DORITOS

Eden said she still lifts weights a little. "Not as heavy as I used to." She added that weightlifting is especially good for women and their bones.

The actress also has a simple beauty routine which she said is what she’s always done. It involves washing her face at night and putting on moisturizer.

"That's about it," she revealed.

One thing the timeless beauty said she wished she had known about when she was younger was "the damage the sun could do to your skin. We didn't know that when I was growing up. And I think it really helps, if you know, to put sunscreen, you know, on your face during the day. Or if you're working."

item.title: UCLA's quarterback made one of the worst plays of the season, and it might cost the Bruins a CFB playoff spot
item.description: Madden Iamaleava's baffling second-overtime blunder left tight end Josh Phifer wide open as the UCLA Bruins fell 18-16 in triple overtime to Michigan.
item.content:encoded:
In a college football season full of surprises, perhaps no team has been a bigger surprise than the UCLA Bruins.

UCLA has languished in relative obscurity for years, despite its location, large recruiting base, and playing home games at the historic Rose Bowl. Known mostly for poor attendance and a string of coaching and athletic department hires, the Bruins finally turned their program around in 2026 by hiring Bob Chesney from James Madison.

Chesney brought many of his JMU players with him, rebuilt the culture around the team, and refocused the offense around a dynamic and unique rushing attack. After a dismal 2025, UCLA started 2026 by racking up wins. And just kept winning. Even after an injury to Nico Iamaleava forced them to turn to backup Ty Dieffenbach, the Bruins handled their, admittedly not extremely difficult, schedule week after week.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S QUIET SATURDAY TURNS INTO A BIG TEN DISASTER WITH BRUTAL CFP CONSEQUENCES

On Saturday, it traveled to Ann Arbor to face the disappointing Michigan Wolverines at The Big House. Two teams known for their defensive prowess and propensity for running the ball played, well, exactly the game you'd expect. Little offense, close, hard fought, and physical hits.

One of those physical plays led to Dieffenbach suffering what appeared to be a serious lower-body injury to his left side, requiring him to be carted off the field. The Bruins went from potentially clinching a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game to staring down the rest of overtime with a third-string quarterback.

With that third-stringer, Madden Iamaleava, now in the game, UCLA kicked a field goal to take a 13-10 lead, then held Michigan to a field goal attempt of their own. It was the second overtime, however, where Iamaleava may have cost his team a chance at the College Football Playoff.

After the Bruins defense once again held the Wolverines to a field goal, the UCLA offense had a chance for a walk-off touchdown to all but guarantee their spot in the 12-team tournament. And they had an opportunity.

On third-and-6 from just past the 21-yard line, Chesney and his staff dialed up the perfect play call. Iamaleava rolled out of the pocket, away from the Michigan defense, and had nothing but green turf in front of him. He also had tight end Josh Phifer a yard past the first down marker, completely uncovered, right in front of his face.

Run forward and it's an easy first down. Throw one of the easiest passes in football, that a Pop Warner quarterback could make, and it's an easy first down for Phifer, who might have found his way into the end zone. Instead? Iamaleava chose...neither.

Instead, he just kinda...stopped running, pointed at something, slowed down, didn't throw the ball at all, and was tackled by linebacker Troy Bowles for a meaningless one-yard gain.

How on earth is this a college quarterback play? How on earth did he not toss the ball to Phifer? Or literally just run forward for the easy first down? How do you choose neither and do nothing? Look at UCLA offensive lineman Carter Sweazie, No. 52, literally pointing for Iamaleava to throw the ball to Phifer. Amazing.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

There's no guarantee that the Bruins convert the easiest first down in football history into a game-ending touchdown, but the atrocious mistake forced them into a field goal to tie it at 16. Sure enough, in the now-mandatory triple overtime two-point conversion attempt, Iamaleava also did...nothing. And Michigan converted to secure the 18-16 win and change UCLA's season.

After the game, Chesney was as magnanimous as a head coach can be under the circumstances.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"It's tough to lose anybody. ... It's the brand, the game that we play," he said. "We all understand that it's really hard to make it through the whole season unscathed. Not the greatest moment to lose him. But at the same point, we have to trust Madden. He's got to be able to deliver in those moments."

Well, he did the opposite. That's one of the worst plays you'll ever see a quarterback make that doesn't result in a turnover.

So why does this jeopardize UCLA's incredible season? The Bruins now head home to host the rival USC Trojans on Saturday. If Dieffenbach can't play, it's clear that Madden Iamaleava is a big liability on offense. And while their running game and defense are outstanding, when teams become one-dimensional offensively, it's a lot easier to stop.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

USC's offense too, despite some struggles, is still one of the better units in the country. If they're able to get out to a fast start and put together a multi-score lead, relying on Iamaleava to bring the Bruins back looks like an unlikely outcome, to say the least.

A loss would give them two, and while that would be enough to make them a top-3 team if they played in the SEC, thanks to being in the Big Ten, it's a near-certainty it pushes them towards the back of the top-12, if not out of it. Especially considered the perceived lack of top opponents. Though they have a win over No. 13 Oregon, several mid-tier teams like Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Illinois, and now play USC, who will likely sit around No. 15-16 when the new rankings hit on Tuesday.

While they still control their destiny to reach the conference championship game in Indianapolis, should they lose to USC, they'd need some other outcomes to go their way to secure a spot. And playing in that championship game might matter, a lot, for the playoff resume.

If they lose, the Oregon Ducks beat Washington, and Iowa and Indiana win, as they'll all be favored to do, they're out. It's hard to believe that UCLA could go from undefeated and No. 4 to out of the playoff entirely in just two weeks, but that's the situation they find themselves in.

Because Madden Iamaleava made one of the worst plays you'll ever see. That's how close the margins are in modern college football. The SC-UCLA rivalry game is already one of the more fun games on the calendar, but the stakes this year are higher than in most recent seasons. Should be must-see TV.

item.title: Famous bald eagle Lincoln goes rogue before Eagles game, takes an unexpected joy flight
item.description: Lincoln, the Budweiser Super Bowl commercial bald eagle, went rogue before the Philadelphia Eagles hosted Pittsburgh Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes, even celebrity bald eagles get the zoomies.

Lincoln, the famous bird who stole hearts in Budweiser's Super Bowl commercial earlier this year, apparently decided to go off-script before the Philadelphia Eagles hosted the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

The 28-year-old bald eagle, who regularly performs ceremonial flyovers at Lincoln Financial Field, seemingly went rogue during his pregame appearance, taking an unexpected detour instead of sticking to his usual flight routine.

Apparently, Lincoln had some extra energy to burn.

And while a bald eagle flying wherever he pleases might sound perfectly normal, Lincoln isn't just any bird.

He's a highly trained performer who has spent years learning to navigate packed football stadiums, television sets and other environments most wild eagles will never encounter.

Back in April, OutKick OutDoors visited the American Eagle Foundation in Kodak, Tenn., where Lincoln lives when he's not entertaining NFL crowds or starring in commercials.

And having met him myself, I can tell you this bird has personality.

There's a certain confidence about him. A lot of attitude. Kind of like he knows America is in love with him.

Lincoln was hatched at the American Eagle Foundation in 1998 and initially released into the wild. But despite flying more than 500 miles in his first two weeks, he struggled to hunt and eventually began seeking out humans to give him food.

Wildlife officials ultimately determined he couldn't survive on his own, so he returned to the foundation, where he became an ambassador for bald eagle conservation.

And, eventually, a pretty big celebrity.

His NFL career began in 2024 after years of specialized training, which allows him to fly freely around a stadium packed with more than 65,000 screaming football fans.

During our visit, American Eagle Foundation avian care specialist Ryn Cobb explained how that process works.

"It's a little complicated, but we basically teach them that food is a rewarding behavior for them," Cobb told OutKick OutDoors. "They understand that when they come to the glove, they get food. And slowly over time, we increase that distance."

So Lincoln isn't tethered during his stadium performances. He's genuinely flying free, and the decision to return to his handler is ultimately his.

"We use a GPS system called telemetry that attaches to his ankle and that keeps him safe so we know where he is," Cobb explained. "And he chooses to come home every single time."

item.title: Democrats clinch historic House majority as Chuck Hubbard defeats longtime GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx
item.description: Democrats secured their largest House majority since 1992, setting up clashes with Trump over investigations, health care and Republican policies.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats have stormed back into power in the House, securing the largest majority of any party since 1992 in a sweeping midterm victory that will reshape the balance of power in Washington and leave Republicans with significantly less influence over the chamber.

The victory was cemented after Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the House from North Carolina, according to The Associated Press (AP). He defeated longtime Republican incumbent Rep. Virginia Foxx, who chaired the powerful House Rules Committee, which determines which bills reach the House floor for a vote.

With several general election results still being called, Democrats have picked up 44 seats so far, giving them at least 258 seats in the House, their largest majority in more than three decades, according to The AP.

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

Meanwhile, Republicans have been left with at least 173 seats.

Four House races remain undecided in Minnesota, Tennessee and two December runoffs in Louisiana, according to The AP.

The party's projected majority will surpass its post-election totals in every election since Bill Clinton first won the presidency in 1992, when Democrats secured 258 seats, the outlet said. The party's next-largest showing reportedly came in 2008, when Barack Obama was elected president and Democrats won 257 House seats.

The shift in the 435-member House will set the stage for a dramatic power struggle in Washington.

WHAT THE 2026 MIDTERM RESULTS MEAN FOR CAPITOL HILL

Democrats are also poised to take control of the Senate, where they secured a 56-seat majority in the 100-member chamber, their largest advantage in more than a decade.

Democrats scored some of their biggest victories in traditionally competitive states and Republican strongholds alike, including Texas, Georgia, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina.

BLUE WAVE NEARLY SWALLOWED SOME OF AMERICA'S REDDEST STATES AS ELECTION DATA EXPOSES GOP'S CLOSE CALLS

President Donald Trump will face a new legislative reality when the next Congress convenes in January, with Democrats preparing to launch a flurry of investigations targeting his administration and its Republican allies in Congress.

The party's 100-day agenda will also focus on rolling back Republican policies, with top priorities including reversing GOP Medicaid cuts and restoring Affordable Care Act tax credits that Republicans allowed to expire, The AP said.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Common sleep habit linked to 50% higher death risk in heart patients, recent study finds
item.description: A PLOS One study of 3,287 US adults with heart disease links sleeping nine or more hours to a 51% higher risk of all-cause mortality over 15 years.
item.content:encoded:
Adults with heart disease who sleep nine or more hours per night could be at a higher risk of death from both heart-related and non-heart-related causes than those who sleep seven to eight hours, according to a recent study.

The cohort study in the journal PLOS One, titled "Sleep duration and cause-specific mortality among US adults with heart disease," analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease from the 2004 National Health Survey linked to the National Death Index running until Dec. 31, 2019.

In the National Health Survey, participants answered whether they had heart disease based on if they had ever been told they had coronary heart disease, a heart attack or a heart condition or disease, according to the study.

MORE NAPS, HIGHER RISK? RESEARCH LINKS DAYTIME SLEEP TO HEALTH WARNINGS IN AGING ADULTS

"Sleep affects blood pressure, blood sugar regulation, inflammation, and appetite hormones, and all of these influence cardiovascular risk," Erin Palinksi-Wade, a New Jersey-based registered dietitian and Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist (CDCES), told Fox News Digital.

The study authors adjusted for health factors and lifestyle behaviors such as body mass index (BMI), alcohol consumption, smoking, physical activity, diabetes, hypertension and more.

Sleep per 24 hours was categorized into durations of six hours or less, seven to eight hours and nine or more hours.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Over approximately 15 years of follow-up, 49.4% of participants died.

Out of all participants, 16.7% died from heart-related causes and 32.6% died from non-heart-related causes.

After adjusting for all lifestyle factors, researchers found that sleeping nine or more hours was linked to a higher mortality risk, compared with sleeping seven to eight hours.

There was a 51% increased risk of all causes of death, a 53% increased risk of heart-related causes of death and a 50% increased risk of non-heart-related mortality.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Sleep duration of six hours or less was significantly associated with non-heart-related death only in the least-adjusted model, and the connection weakened with further adjustment.

"Because the study is observational, it shows an association, not cause and effect. Long sleep may be a symptom of underlying problems like more advanced heart disease, depression, sleep apnea, or medication side effects, and the study couldn't fully account for those," Palinski-Wade said.

The authors noted that their findings do not invalidate the negative cardiovascular effects of getting too little sleep.

"I'm not aware of a convincing biological mechanism by which extra hours of sleep damage the heart," Antony Chu, MD, a cardiologist and clinical assistant professor at Brown University’s Warren Alpert School of Medicine, told Fox News Digital.

"What I see clinically is that patients sleep longer because something is pulling on their reserve: worsening heart failure, untreated obstructive or central sleep apnea, depression, sedating medications, anemia or frailty," Chu said.

Sleeping too much or too little are both potential red flags, Palinski-Wade noted, so it’s important for people to pay attention to how rested they feel rather than only focusing on the number of hours they slept.

Because the study only tested people with pre-existing heart conditions, it should not be used to suggest that prolonged sleep leads to heart disease in the general population, she added.

item.title: Massive 17-foot shark comes face-to-face with scientists in incredible deep-sea footage
item.description: Viral video captures a massive bluntnose sixgill shark pressing her snout against a submersible window 1,700 feet beneath the Atlantic near the Bahamas.
item.content:encoded:
A video making the rounds on social media Sunday shows a massive deep-water shark getting up close and personal with a group of scientists inside a submersible.

And when I say up close and personal, I mean it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

In the footage, the shark slowly circles the vessel, seemingly just as curious about its human visitors as they are about her. At one point, she swims right up to the viewing window and presses her snout against the glass.

The video is spectacular, but it isn't new. The encounter actually happened back in June 2019, roughly 1,700 feet beneath the surface of the Atlantic Ocean near the Bahamas.

Check out the piercing blue eye at the 52-second mark.

The shark is a bluntnose sixgill, a deep-water species that can grow up to 20 feet long. Researchers estimated that the particularly inquisitive female in the video measured about 16-17 feet.

And as incredible as the footage is, the story behind it might be even cooler.

The encounter occurred during an expedition by OceanX, an ocean exploration organization working alongside marine scientists to study the bluntnose sixgill shark.

The team traveled to the deep waters of Exuma Sound aboard the research vessel Alucia, hoping to accomplish something that had never been done before: attach a satellite tracking tag to a sixgill shark without bringing it to the surface.

THE BIGGEST NAMES AND WILDEST STORIES IN THE GREAT OUTDOORS. WATCH 'OPEN SEASON' ON YOUTUBE!

Previously, researchers studying these animals had to capture them and haul them up from the depths. But that process can stress the sharks and disrupt their natural behavior, making it difficult to collect reliable data about how they actually live.

Using OceanX's three-person submersible, Nadir, the team descended into the darkness with roughly 100 pounds of bait to attract the sharks.

After several unsuccessful attempts involving bad weather, equipment problems and even a grouper that interfered with the tagging process, the researchers finally got their chance on June 29.

According to the Florida Museum of Natural History, scientist Gavin Naylor successfully attached a satellite tag to a male sixgill shark more than 1,700 feet underwater.

It was the first time scientists had successfully tagged one at depth in its natural habitat.

But the team also encountered several other sharks during the dive, including the enormous female that stars in the viral video.

FORREST GALANTE SAYS MOST SHARK BITES ARE A CASE OF MISTAKEN IDENTITY AS FLORIDA ATTACKS LEAD THE US

"She was studying us," Naylor told the Florida Museum. "It was delightful for me to see a shark being curious. We'd be arrogant to think we were the only ones doing the evaluating."

Bluntnose sixgill sharks are among the largest predatory sharks in the ocean, although most people will never see one. That's because these animals spend much of their lives hundreds or even thousands of feet below the surface. Some have been documented at depths approaching 6,500 feet.

They're also pretty much living fossils. According to the Florida Museum, sixgills closely resemble sharks that swam the oceans roughly 200 million years ago.

Way down there, sixgills aren't generally a threat to humans. They spend their days hunting fish, squid and other marine life, occasionally scavenging larger carcasses.

And considering how little we still know about what goes on in the depths of our oceans, it's pretty fascinating to think about what else might be lurking down there.

Fascinating and utterly terrifying.

item.title: Jim Beam to pause production at flagship Kentucky distillery in major shift for iconic American whiskey brand
item.description: Jim Beam shifts bourbon production to its Booker Noe Distillery in Boston, Kentucky, as whiskey inventory hits three times annual U.S. demand, per IWSR.
item.content:encoded:
Jim Beam will indefinitely pause production at its historic flagship distillery in Clermont, Kentucky, amid declining whiskey sales and record inventories.

The iconic American whiskey brand, owned by Japanese multinational brewing and distilling company Suntory Global Spirits, announced last December that it would pause production at its Clermont, Kentucky facility for one year, with plans to resume operations in 2027, Food Dive reported.

However, in a new development, it is now uncertain when the Clermont distillery will begin operations again, the company told The Courier Journal.

NEW 123.4-PROOF WHISKEY PROMPTS EXPERT WARNING THAT STRONGER ISN'T ALWAYS BETTER

Suntory told the outlet that it manages its Kentucky production in accordance with demand, inventory and long-term needs.

The company noted that it plans to reassess production needs in the future.

In the meantime, Jim Beam has moved production to its nearby Booker Noe Distillery in Boston, Kentucky, which, with an output of 45 million original proof gallons annually, is the brand’s largest distillery, according to Food Dive.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The brand's Fred B. Noe distillery, located on the Clermont facility's campus, will continue its operations producing whiskey labels including Knob Creek, Little Book and Booker's, Inc. reported.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jim Beam and the brand’s parent company, Suntory Holdings, for comment.

Jim Beam’s move comes amid an ongoing decrease in consumer demand for whiskey, with large quantities of the spirit sitting untouched.

Whiskey inventory in the U.S. is three times higher than estimated annual demand, global beverage alcohol data and insight firm IWSR reported in October.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"The unifying theme across Scotch, US, Japanese and Irish whiskey is polarisation by price tier: we are seeing growth narrowing to specific bands within each whisky sub-category, rather than spreading across the price ladder," said Marten Lodewijks, IWSR managing director and president.

"And in most cases, that growth is concentrating at the premium end, while the mainstream and value tiers absorb the pain," he added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Members of the Kentucky Distillers Association held an inventory of 16.1 million barrels of whiskey as of October 2025, according to the organization’s website.

Total beverage alcohol sales declined for the third consecutive year in 2025, according to IWSR.

item.title: Noah’s Ark search team says wood near Mount Ararat dates to 4,300 years ago, in line with biblical flood
item.description: Andrew Jones says lab results date wood from a Noah's Ark site near Mount Ararat to about 4,300 years ago, lining up with the biblical flood.
item.content:encoded:
The founder of a team searching for Noah’s Ark in Turkey says initial lab results have dated the wood recovered from the site to approximately 4,300 years ago, a timeline he says lines up with traditional dates for when the biblical flood occurred.

"We can announce that the samples date back to about 4,300 years ago, so this lines up with some of the traditional dates for the flood of Noah," Andrew Jones said on "Saturday in America." "So we're in the right time period."

Jones said the Noah's Ark Scans team recovered several bags of what he described as "burnt-looking wood." Other pieces of wood collected from the site, located near Mount Ararat, bore markings consistent with tool work.

NOAH'S ARK SITE YIELDS FIRST LOOK AT CHARRED WOOD FRAGMENTS RECOVERED DEEP BELOW SOIL

The samples were found 30 feet underground on the western side of what Jones called a "boat formation," which he said is about 300 cubits long — matching the size of the ark described in the Bible.

AUTHOR DINESH D'SOUZA CHALLENGES BIBLE SKEPTICS WITH 'STARTLING' ARCHAEOLOGICAL DISCOVERIES

"What we don't know is how the wood got there. And so we're doing it one step at a time, but we're happy to see this initial results from one of the labs."

Jones said he believes he is studying the real Noah's Ark, adding that his team is "following the scientific evidence."

"We're checking out every piece of evidence that we gather... and reporting the results wherever the data goes."

Jones said interest in the site first began more than 65 years ago when the boat formation was discovered near the place the Bible says Noah's Ark landed. His claims, however, contradict the scientific consensus that the site is merely a natural rock formation.

Despite some opposition to the excavation, Jones said one professor he is working with was impressed by the public interest.

"The professor said he was amazed, that he's never been on a project like this where people care so much about archaeology that they want to try to stop us, thinking we're destroying the site," Jones said.

item.title: Wild trail cam footage shows buck protecting a doe by tossing a bobcat giving chase with its antlers
item.description: Trail camera footage from Georgia captures a bobcat chasing a doe before a buck charges in, tossing the predator through the air with its antlers.
item.content:encoded:
Chivalry is alive and well and this trail camera footage from the wilderness in Georgia proves it. The video shows a bobcat pursuing a doe before a buck steps between them.

The buck wasn't about to let the bobcat get close enough to attack the doe. A doe can be seen running out of the trees on one side of a small clearing into the trees on the other side.

After the doe disappears into the woods, a buck emerges out of the trees nearby. It turns and starts heading towards the trail camera. As it does, a bobcat can be seen stepping out from the trees.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

The bobcat stops dead in its tracks after noticing the buck was eyeing it. There's a brief standoff as the two animals size each other up. The buck gives a couple of stomps with its front legs then charges.

This is where the video goes full National Geographic. The bobcat attempts to jump on the buck and is tossed through the air. The buck used its head and antlers to send the bobcat flying.

TWO MASSIVE ELK LOCK ANTLERS IN FEISTY COLORADO FIGHT CAPTURED ON STUNNING WILDLIFE FOOTAGE

It's at that point that the bobcat decides that it wasn't all that hungry after all and the doe isn't worth the effort or the antlers.

It runs off, the buck gives chase, and at least as far as the matter is concerned in this footage, the doe is safe.

The little pump fake by the bobcat didn't fool the buck at all. This wasn’t going to be a playful exchange.

The buck saw the move from a mile away and charged immediately. The bobcat should have known better once the buck headed its way.

Perhaps it fell for the claim that chivalry was dead and thought it could chase the buck off and force it to leave his lady unprotected. That was not the case.

item.title: FDA clears tiny surgical robot to remove bladder tumors
item.description: The FDA-authorized Virtuoso Endoscopy System uses needle-sized robotic arms to remove bladder tumors intact, helping pathologists assess detrusor muscle.
item.content:encoded:
If a doctor finds a tumor in your bladder, you want to know what you're dealing with. Is it cancer? Has it reached the bladder muscle? The tissue removed during surgery helps answer those questions. Now, a tiny surgical robot could give doctors a clearer view of what's happening inside the bladder.

The FDA has authorized the Virtuoso Endoscopy System, developed by Nashville-based Virtuoso Surgical. It uses two needle-sized robotic arms to remove bladder lesions through the urethra, without cutting through the skin. The technology allows surgeons to remove many tumors in one piece, potentially giving pathologists better tissue samples to examine. This new approach to robotic bladder tumor removal could help doctors make more informed treatment decisions.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

WOULD YOU TRUST A TINY DENTAL ROBOT?

The Virtuoso Endoscopy System uses a narrow medical instrument called a rigid endoscope, which enters the bladder through the urethra. At the tip are two miniature robotic arms made from a flexible metal alloy called nitinol. A surgeon controls both arms from a console. One arm lifts and holds the tumor while the other carefully separates it from the tissue underneath. This gives the surgeon two-handed control inside a very small space.

The technique is called en bloc resection, which means removing a tumor in one piece. Surgeons can already perform this procedure using conventional instruments, but it can be technically demanding. Virtuoso designed its system to make that approach easier to perform. The robot also relies entirely on the surgeon's movements. Unlike some autonomous surgical robots being tested in research settings, Virtuoso does not make surgical decisions or operate independently.

Bladder cancer affects thousands of Americans every year. The American Cancer Society estimates that approximately 84,530 people in the United States will receive a bladder cancer diagnosis in 2026. One of the most common procedures for evaluating and removing bladder tumors is called transurethral resection of bladder tumor, or TURBT. During conventional TURBT, surgeons often remove tumors in smaller fragments. While effective for many patients, that approach can disrupt the tissue's original structure. As a result, pathologists may have a harder time determining how deeply cancer has grown. That's particularly important when it comes to the bladder's muscle layer, called the detrusor muscle. Doctors need to know whether cancer has reached this muscle because that can change the recommended treatment.

Removing a lesion intact may preserve more of the information pathologists need. It can also allow them to examine the tissue around the tumor more clearly. Dr. Duke Herrell, a urologic surgeon and CEO of Virtuoso Surgical, explained the potential benefit in the company's FDA announcement. "Removing a tumor intact can provide a better tissue specimen, which supports clearer diagnosis and staging," Herrell said. For patients, a more complete tissue sample could help their medical team determine the next steps with greater confidence.

Virtuoso has already tested the system in human patients, and the early clinical findings are encouraging. In the first 20 patients enrolled in the company-sponsored VIABLE study at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, 94% of removed lesions contained detrusor muscle. That exceeded the study's predefined performance goal of 60%. Researchers also reported that surgical margins could be evaluated in 93% of malignant lesions. Surgical margins are the edges of the removed tissue. Examining them can help doctors assess whether cancer cells extend to the edge of the sample. However, being able to evaluate a margin does not necessarily mean it is free of cancer. The company reported no adverse events during the operations.

There are important limitations to these findings. The study involved a small number of patients at one medical center. The previously published first phase of the same VIABLE study involved six patients and recorded two postoperative adverse events. One patient experienced temporary urinary retention, while another developed a chest infection later linked to a separate esophageal tumor. The company also compared its results with previously published research on conventional bladder tumor removal.

However, the Virtuoso study did not directly compare the robot against traditional instruments in a randomized trial. Researchers still need larger studies to determine whether the system improves long-term outcomes or reduces the need for additional procedures.

BRAIN TUMOR FOUND DURING PREVENTIVE SCAN PUTS FULL-BODY MRIS BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT

The FDA granted De Novo authorization for the Virtuoso Endoscopy System on Oct. 30, 2026. The company publicly announced the decision on Nov. 10. The authorization establishes a new FDA classification for robotic surgical instruments that operate through an endoscope inside the body. Specifically, the system is authorized to remove bladder lesions in adult patients and obtain tissue samples, including bladder muscle, to assist in diagnosing bladder cancer.

The decision follows the FDA's September 2025 Breakthrough Device Designation for the system. That earlier designation recognized the technology's potential and allowed the company to receive additional regulatory guidance during development. However, the new authorization does not establish that the robot improves survival rates or prevents cancer from returning. The system must also be operated by trained surgeons in an operating room.

Virtuoso Surgical plans a limited U.S. launch in 2027, starting with leading urology centers. The company has not announced which hospitals will receive the system first. That means patients may have to wait before the technology becomes available at their local hospital. Questions also remain about pricing and insurance coverage.

Virtuoso is exploring other potential applications for its miniature robotic instruments, including procedures involving the lungs. However, those uses remain experimental and have not received FDA authorization. For now, the company's focus is bladder surgery, where better tissue samples could help doctors evaluate cancer more accurately.

If you or someone you love is facing bladder cancer, this technology could eventually provide another surgical option. Its miniature robotic arms may help doctors obtain more complete tissue samples during the initial procedure. However, availability will be limited at first, and the early results still need confirmation in larger studies. The robot's FDA authorization also does not guarantee better results for every patient.

If you're discussing bladder tumor surgery with a urologist, ask whether en bloc resection might be appropriate for your situation. You should also ask how the surgeon plans to obtain enough tissue to determine whether cancer has reached the bladder muscle. Those answers can help you understand your options before surgery.

When you're facing a possible cancer diagnosis, getting accurate answers as early as possible can make a real difference. That's what I like about this technology. Virtuoso's tiny robotic arms could help surgeons collect better tissue samples without taking control away from the medical professional performing the operation. It's also encouraging to see the FDA authorize a system designed for such a specific surgical challenge. Still, 20 patients represent a very small study, and I want to see how this robot performs in larger trials before getting too excited about its potential. If the results hold up, this could become a valuable addition to the tools doctors use to diagnose bladder cancer.

Would you trust a surgeon using this new robotic system to remove a tumor, or would you prefer a conventional procedure until there's more evidence of its benefits? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com
